clue.text: One gets drinks supply during Prohibition

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a prohibition is a ban
to arm is to supply, as with weapons

explanation.surface: Someone keeps the drink flowing during the American Prohibition era, like a bootlegger.
explanation.walkthrough: Prohibition with a capital P evokes 1920s America, but it is just a ban, with ARM placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman is the person behind a bar who pours and serves customers their drinks.

clue.text: Wife leaves fool for friend

indicators.note: when someone leaves, they are no longer there, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a silly person
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife walks out on a foolish husband and takes up with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLY is British slang for an idiot; drop its W and ALLY remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone on your side, a supporter or companion, much as a friend is.

clue.text: Picture buff doctor that is pursuing lover essentially promising proposal

indicators.note: to pursue is to come after, so the preceding words follow the next piece

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a military doctor

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the five-letter word
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
a goer is an idea or plan likely to succeed

explanation.surface: A doctor's lover makes a promising proposal of marriage, like a romantic film plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' here means a film, as in going to the pictures. IE follows the V because 'that is' is pursuing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A moviegoer regularly goes to the cinema, so is an enthusiast for films, which are also called pictures.

clue.text: Bagel not having "gross" filling

indicators.note: having something means holding it, so one word takes the other inside
a filling sits in the middle, as jam does in a doughnut, so these letters go within

parts.note: taken as written
ugh is the exclamation for something gross or disgusting

explanation.surface: A bagel that has no unpleasant filling in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' suggests the bagel's contents, and the quotation marks around 'gross' hint that it stands for an exclamation of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis slang a bagel is a set lost six games to love, so it stands for zero, as its ring shape suggests.

clue.text: 10 mice fish, extraordinarily

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mice that fish would be a strange sight indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 10 across, INJURY: to do someone a mischief is to hurt them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief can mean harm or damage done to someone, as in the phrase do yourself a mischief.

clue.text: Economists are travelling across America delivering great news

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the surrounding letters go around the other piece
things that travel move about, so these letters shift into new places

parts.note: taken as written
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: Economists touring the United States bring a welcome economic report.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters wrap around US, which sits just after the opening M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is music to one's ears is very welcome to hear, an idiom for good news.

clue.text: Big energy rises possible to apprehend

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means moving higher up the column, so that letter is lifted out and put back nearer the top

parts.note: sizeable means large; the spelling with an E is the one used
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A large amount of energy goes up, perhaps enough to capture.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the E out of the middle of SIZEABLE and put it back higher, after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Seizable describes something that can be seized, and to seize a person is to arrest or catch them.

clue.text: Veil three consecutive letters and then two more

indicators.note: and then means one thing follows straight after another, so the pieces join in order

parts.note: three letters running in alphabetical order
two further letters, the first pair of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone composing a veil out of a string of alphabet letters, like a word puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Any run of three would fit the wordplay, so the definition must choose it: HIJ followed by AB, the alphabet's first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijab is the headscarf or veil worn by many Muslim women to cover the hair.

clue.text: Beethoven's hearing aid reduced temperature somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unknown way of arranging, so the letters are rearranged
reduced means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The deaf composer's hearing device somehow lowered the temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven grew deaf and used several of these horn-shaped devices, so he serves as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear trumpet is the old cone-shaped device held to the ear to amplify sound, used by the deaf composer.

clue.text: Smacks boundaries around cricket ground after opener is dismissed from behind

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: in cricket a boundary scores four runs

indicators.note: read from behind means read from the back, so the letters run backwards
in cricket the opener goes in first, and dismissing it removes the first letter

parts.note: the Oval is a London cricket ground

explanation.surface: A batsman hits boundaries around the ground after the opening batter is out to a catch behind the stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket throughout: the Oval is a London Test ground, a boundary is worth four, and 'after' is a link, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a distinctive taste or trace, as in smacks of garlic, so smacks are tastes.

clue.text: Where Foreman could be hurt

definitions.note: read as two words, in jury
definitions.meaning: a jury has a foreman, so he could be in the jury

definitions.note: a noun here, as in a hurt or wound

explanation.surface: Wondering where the boxer George Foreman might take a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F points to the boxer George Foreman, but this foreman leads a jury: split the answer as IN JURY.
explanation.definitionFit: An injury is damage done to the body, which is what a hurt is when used as a noun.

clue.text: What the definition here doesn't yet do for narrow-minded groups online

definitions.text: What the definition here doesn't yet do
definitions.note: read as two words, echo Chambers
definitions.meaning: the Chambers dictionary does not yet carry this modern sense, so the definition does not repeat what Chambers says
the definition proper, a modern internet term

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is the dictionary crossword setters use; the clue jokes that its definition of the answer is not yet in it, so it cannot repeat the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo chambers are online communities where people hear only views like their own, reinforcing a closed outlook.

clue.text: Discover former lover carrying ecstasy on a street in Seven Sisters area

indicators.note: in a down entry one thing sitting on another goes above it, so these letters come first

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street
to suss something out is to discover it
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Finding an ex-partner on a street carrying drugs in a seaside region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Seven Sisters are chalk cliffs on the south coast of England; the county is a region of English local government.
explanation.definitionFit: East Sussex is the English county on the south coast containing the Seven Sisters chalk cliffs.

clue.text: It's become pudding

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
to go can mean to become, as in go mad

explanation.surface: Something has turned into a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal is a crossword favourite: someone who has it is attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith, boiled with milk to make a traditional British milk pudding.

clue.text: OK Computer overshadowed by a second big hit when making a comeback

definitions.note: the US postal abbreviation of the state

indicators.note: a comeback runs the other way, so the assembled letters are read backwards
being overshadowed by something puts it in front, so those letters precede the first piece

parts.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second
HAL is the computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey
a knockout, the knockout blow in boxing

explanation.surface: Radiohead's album OK Computer is outsold by a big hit second album as the band returns.
explanation.walkthrough: OK Computer is a Radiohead album, but OK is the definition and Computer is HAL; A MO HAL KO is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: OK is the two-letter postal abbreviation of Oklahoma, a state in the south-central United States.

clue.text: Down at heel half-hearted rogue in piece of cloth

indicators.note: a rogue goes astray and behaves unpredictably, so the letters are scrambled
losing half its heart means one of the two middle letters is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shabby, half-hearted scoundrel dressed in rags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down at heel' reads as shabby and 'rogue' as a villain; in fact HEEL loses one middle E and the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand towel is a small towel for drying the hands, which is a piece of absorbent fabric.

clue.text: Loomed over current politician in the van

indicators.note: the van is the vanguard, the front, so these letters lead

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a Member of Parliament
when something is over it has ended

explanation.surface: A sitting politician in a van looms over us, like an election campaign vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loomed over' looks like one phrase, but 'over' is ENDED and 'van' means front, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Impended means was about to happen in a threatening way, just as an event that loomed was close and menacing.

clue.text: North American primarily overseeing the shop counter

definitions.text: North American primarily overseeing the shop counter

parts.words: North American primarily overseeing the shop counter
parts.note: surface reading: an American shopkeeper who runs the till; setter's reading: the person who counts stock in a store, a word primarily North American for a shop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like the shop's serving counter but means one who counts: the man who keeps inventory in the store.
explanation.definitionFit: A storeman looks after and counts the goods held in a warehouse or stockroom; store is the American word for shop.

clue.text: Must hit balls with purpose when being broadcast?

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to knee someone in the groin is a deliberate blow

explanation.surface: A sportsman must strike the ball purposefully when the match is televised.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitting balls suggests sport, but here it is a deliberate knee to the groin.
explanation.definitionFit: Must and need both express obligation, as in you must go or you need to go.

clue.text: Oscar engaged in level game

indicators.note: being engaged in something means being involved inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: being quits means being even, all square
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner is engaged to someone on an equal footing.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar suggests the film award, but it is the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits is a traditional game of throwing rings over a peg, often played on ships' decks.

clue.text: Fancy dress functions in circuit clubs, perhaps

definitions.note: fancy is a verb here: to fancy dress is a wish, and the suit is the dress

indicators.note: in places one thing within another, so the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a bus is a circuit route, and a bus is also a circuit conductor in electronics
sines are trigonometric functions
clubs is one of the four suits in cards

explanation.surface: Elaborate costumes worn at events in nightclubs on the club circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy dress' suggests a costume party; read it as formal attire. In electronics a bus is a circuit of conductors.
explanation.definitionFit: A business suit is a formal jacket and trousers worn to work, an outfit of formal clothing for the office.

clue.text: Birdie regularly, eagle periodically — perfect!

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

indicators.note: periodically means at intervals, so again alternate letters are kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A golfer's round with birdies and occasional eagles would be ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a birdie is one under par and an eagle two under, but here they only supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless and exactly as one would wish, matching the exclamation perfect.

clue.text: Trace car from 1966

definitions.meaning: British registration plates once carried a year letter

explanation.walkthrough: UK number plates used a suffix letter for the year of registration, and D marked cars registered in 1966 to 1967.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreg is the smallest remaining amount of something, a residue, as in not a dreg of sympathy.

clue.text: Sailor bound to drink nip of tawny port

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
a bound is a limit or end

indicators.note: a nip is a tiny taste, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the initial letter

explanation.surface: A sailor is bound to have a nip of tawny port.
explanation.walkthrough: Tawny port is a wine, but here port is the definition: a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian ferry and fishing port on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: If you will raise tons, we will perform

indicators.note: a performance turns material into something new, so these letters are worked into another order

parts.note: taken as written
t is the abbreviation for tons
taken as written

explanation.surface: If you raise lots of money, we will do the show.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were and if you will are both phrases that apologise for an unusual or figurative choice of words.

clue.text: Sees red liberal wearing old school tie finally succeeded

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: something worn is inside what wears it, so one letter sits within the other piece

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter
s is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage when a liberal turns up in an old school tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old school tie' reads as one phrase but splits three ways; L goes inside POD.
explanation.definitionFit: Explodes and sees red both describe suddenly becoming furious, flying into an uncontrolled rage.

clue.text: Unlimited legitimate retreats providing food fit for animals

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the letters run in reverse
with no limits the word loses its boundaries, its first and last letters

parts.note: to legitimate something is to make it lawful

explanation.surface: Legal shelters provide decent food for livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legitimate' looks like an adjective, but it is a verb meaning to make lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is fermented grass or fodder crops stored to feed cattle and sheep over winter.
